newsitem.title: SYRIA: Survivors describe horror of Damascus bus bombing.
newsitem.headline: Survivors describe horror of Damascus bus bombing.

text.p: Survivors of a bus bombing in Syria described on Friday the horror of an explosion in central Damascus that killed nine people and injured 44 on New Year's Eve.
Israel condemned what it called the "terrorist attack" and rejected Syrian accusations that Israeli agents planted the bomb as an "outright lie".
Speaking to Reuters from their hospital beds, some survivors said a huge blast was followed by a ball of fire that engulfed the stricken bus shortly after noon on Tuesday.

Mohammed Osou, a 22-year-old soldier who had just got a leave from his Damascus-based unit and prepared to travel for the northern city of Aleppo to join his family to celebrate the New Year, arrived a bit late at the station and was among the last to board the bus.
The delay probably saved his life.
"The only empty place was in the back seat and the explosion took place in the middle of the bus at the luggage place...That is why I survived with light wounds," Osou said.
Ramadan Sido, 36, said he was walking near the bus station thinking about the presents he wanted to buy his seven children for the celebrations.
"Suddenly a big explosion rocked the place and something... slapped my face," he said. "I saw a huge ball of fire...I thought there was a termor and it was my end."
Sido, who suffered a broken hand, said he thought nobody would care to take him to hospital at the time of the explosion as the number of those with severe wounds was huge.
"But everybody on the scene rushed for help. All taxis and cars and other vehicles in the area offered to take us to hospitals," he said.
The Israeli cabinet said in a statement after its weekly meeting on Friday: "We unequivocally condemn terrorist actions in Syria and any place.

"The Prime Minister (Benjamin Netanyahu) said that the accusations published in Damascus accusing Israel of responsibility for terrorist attacks in Syria are an outright lie. We have no connection to the terrorist attack in Syria and Syria knows it," the statement said.
Damascus, reporting the bombing for the first time on Thursday, said Israeli agents were behind the blast and hinted the incident was linked to attacks against Syrian targets in Lebanon last month.
France condemned the bombing and expressed hope that those behind it would be quickly identified. The United States warned Syria against making "wild and irresponsible" accusations.

"This is a criminal action that any human being should be ashamed of. Those responsible should be punished because they want to destabilise our peaceful life," Ihsan Jaafar, a 27-year-old computer engineer who was on the bus, said.
His father Nihad Jaafar, sitting at his bedside, said:
"We spent the New Year's Eve in hospital with our son and our family was scattered in two places...It was a sad end to the year. I wish no other father would have the same experience."
